problem: Egocentric hand-object parsing in egocentric video remains limited by transformer models that struggle with object-adaptive query initialization, interaction-irrelevant features, and physically inconsistent predictions.
approach: InterFormer integrates a Dynamic Query Generator for interaction-grounded query initialization, a Dual-context Feature Selector to suppress noise, and a Conditional Co-occurrence loss to enforce hand-object relationship constraints.
contribution: The method addresses three key limitations in transformer-based egocentric interaction understanding through specialized components for query generation and feature selection.

problem: Current understanding of visual neuron selectivity assumes neurons respond primarily to single preferred stimuli, but this model may be incomplete for understanding higher-order visual cortex.
approach: The study empirically characterizes response distributions of V4 neurons and finds evidence for both preferred and anti-preferred stimuli through physiological experiments and psychophysical tasks.
contribution: Demonstrates that V4 neurons exhibit two-tailed response distributions with functionally distinct preferred and anti-preferred stimuli, doubling the feature selectivity capacity of the population.

problem: Federated learning systems with heterogeneous client data distributions focus on aggregation but underexplore how the server can actively guide task allocation to optimize for both local model quality and new query placement.
approach: Proposes a density ratio model and empirical likelihood framework that simultaneously learns effective local models while guiding task allocation to the best-matching client.
contribution: Introduces a novel FL paradigm treating heterogeneity as a feature, achieving improvements in model accuracy and client guidance precision compared to standard approaches.

problem: Temporal Knowledge Graph reasoning focuses on entity-level correlations but overlooks heterogeneous causal relationships embedded in event-level structures, limiting event prediction accuracy.
approach: HEDRA disentangles event-level causalities through counterfactual detection for non-causality, instrumental variables for spurious causality, and evolutionary orthogonality for dynamic vs. static causality.
contribution: First method to explicitly disentangle heterogeneous event-level causalities in TKGs, achieving state-of-the-art performance on five real-world datasets.

problem: Optical music recognition lacks large-scale pretrained models capable of recognizing full-page typeset scores and generating human-readable symbolic notation.
approach: Legato combines a pretrained vision encoder with an ABC notation decoder trained on 214K+ images to perform end-to-end typeset music recognition.
contribution: First large-scale pretrained OMR model achieving 68% absolute error reduction on TEDn and 47.6% on OMR-NED metrics while generating concise ABC notation.

problem: On-policy RLVR frameworks for LLM post-training suffer from experience waste and reward homogeneity, reducing efficiency on difficult reasoning tasks.
approach: BAPO uses off-policy learning to dynamically select batches by re-evaluating historically difficult samples while reusing high-quality ones, with policy improvement guarantees.
contribution: Achieves 12.5% average improvement over GRPO across mathematics, planning, and visual reasoning, resolving 40.7% of problems that base models consistently fail on.

problem: RAG systems enhance LLM performance but expose sensitive user queries and confidential documents, requiring privacy-preserving retrieval mechanisms.
approach: Pisces uses cryptography-based methods with coarse-to-fine semantic retrieval, oblivious filtering, and multi-instance labeled PSI for BM25 scoring while protecting queries and documents.
contribution: First practical cryptography-based RAG framework achieving retrieval accuracy within 1.87% of plaintext baselines while preserving privacy for dual-path retrieval.

problem: Optical flow, scene flow, and stereo benchmarks focus on accuracy but fail to quantify robustness to real-world image corruptions like noise, blur, and weather distortions.
approach: RobustSpring creates a benchmark applying 20 corruption types in time-, stereo-, and depth-consistent manner to 10,000 Spring dataset images, enabling robustness-accuracy trade-off analysis.
contribution: Introduces comprehensive corruption robustness metric and dataset revealing wide variation in model robustness across corruption types, with evidence that RobustSpring indicates real-world resilience.

problem: Meta-reinforcement learning meta-priors show imbalanced generalization, adapting well to some tasks while performing poorly on others, limiting practical utility.
approach: A two-stage approach identifies critical training tasks relevant to poorly adapted tasks using conditional mutual information, then augments critical tasks via bilevel optimization.
contribution: Theoretically guarantees O(1/sqrt(K)) convergence and proves generalization improvement after task augmentation across MuJoCo and Meta-World experiments.

problem: Chemical reaction condition recommendation with LLMs lacks interpretable justifications, limiting applicability in high-stakes scientific workflows requiring explainability.
approach: ChemMAS decomposes condition prediction into mechanistic grounding, multi-channel recall, constraint-aware debate, and rationale aggregation via multi-agent reasoning.
contribution: Achieves 20-35% gains over domain-specific baselines and 10-15% over general LLMs while providing falsifiable, human-trustable rationales for recommended conditions.

problem: Extending LLM context window requires expensive finetuning beyond pretraining sequence length, preventing practical zero-shot context extension.
approach: DroPE removes positional embeddings after pretraining during a short recalibration phase, leveraging the finding that explicit positional information hinders length generalization.
contribution: Enables seamless zero-shot context extension without long-context finetuning, outperforming rotary position embedding scaling methods across different model sizes.

problem: Compositional generalization research lacks controlled testbeds that isolate spatial transfer (systematicity across environments) from length scaling (productivity along difficulty).
approach: A map-navigation testbed separates dimensions of generalization, showing transfer requires sufficient diverse questions while scaling requires exposure to longer examples via RL and SFT.
contribution: Provides principled insights that transfer needs high coverage and modest diversity while scaling critically depends on neighboring-but-longer examples, with RL stabilizing but not exceeding SFT ceilings.

problem: Vision-Language Navigation agents struggle with spatial reasoning in unseen environments due to reliance on explicit semantic memory like textual maps and frame caches.
approach: JanusVLN uses dual implicit neural memory for spatial-geometric and visual-semantic encodings, with shifted SSMs to aggregate historical KV caches from initial and sliding windows.
contribution: Achieves SOTA on VLN with 10.5-35.5% success rate improvements over recent methods by enabling efficient long-term trajectory modeling with compact implicit representations.

problem: Evaluating generated test case quality requires expensive scoring on large unstructured code collections, leading to high computational costs and benchmark inflation favoring trivial bug detection.
approach: Formulates benchmark construction as finding an optimal diagnostic basis in a binary code-test matrix, where rank specifies minimum error patterns and test cases needed.
contribution: Introduces novel framework using matrix rank for efficient benchmark construction that maximizes internal diversity and identifies minimal sufficient wrong codes and test cases.

problem: Solving heterogeneous PDEs requires expensive offline computation of spectral basis functions in multiscale finite element methods, limiting practical scalability.
approach: GMsFEM-NO trains neural operators to predict GMsFEM basis functions using a subspace-informed loss that learns the entire relevant subspace, not just individual functions.
contribution: Reduces solution error compared to standalone neural operators while accelerating GMsFEM's costly offline stage, with discretization flexibility enabling grid-size independent evaluation.

problem: Evaluating chemistry LLMs on molecular properties requires methods beyond literature labels prone to leakage; models must reason faithfully over molecular graph structure.
approach: MolecularIQ creates a benchmark spanning molecular complexity, multi-task load, and reasoning complexity with symbolically verifiable tasks on feature counting and constrained generation.
contribution: Enables fine-grained evaluation revealing that large MoE models lead while chemistry-tuned LLMs underperform generalist bases, indicating limited structural reasoning transfer.

problem: Selective classification via abstention requires new approaches for covariate shift scenarios where test input distribution differs from training, underexplored in prior work.
approach: Applies the Neyman-Pearson lemma to formalize optimal rejection as a likelihood ratio test, proposing new likelihood-ratio-based selection methods for covariate shift.
contribution: Demonstrates that Neyman-Pearson-informed methods consistently outperform existing baselines on vision and language tasks under covariate shifts and for vision-language models.

problem: LLMs as information mediators in social learning create a joint process where agents combine private algorithmic signals with observational learning, raising control and welfare concerns.
approach: Formulates controlled sequential social learning combining dynamic programming with decentralized Bayesian belief updates to characterize optimal altruistic and biased planner policies.
contribution: Proves convexity of value function and reveals that optimal biased planners employ mode-dependent strategies including intentional obfuscation to manipulate agent behavior.

problem: MLLMs exhibit poor diagram understanding and flawed reasoning on diagrams due to weak perceptual capabilities, not reasoning alone, with models resorting to text-based shortcuts.
approach: Develops diagnostic test suite isolating perception from reasoning, revealing that models rely on textual shortcuts and proposing training on graph-primitive structural representations.
contribution: Shows that training on structural representations of diagram primitives and relationships achieves +79% grounding improvement with transfer gains of 3-4% on reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Automated question answering on academic papers lacks comprehensive realistic benchmarks for evaluating LLM agents, and training interactive agents suffers from shortage of quality interaction trajectories.
approach: M4PQA provides 13,948 papers with 1,246 annotated questions spanning multi-task, multi-modal evaluation, while ExTrActor synthesizes instruction trajectories via LLM-based agents without human intervention.
contribution: Demonstrates most models underperform M4PQA; ExTrActor consistently improves small models' tool-use capability to match larger models while enabling instance-level evaluation.

problem: Multi-task learning requires predicting task affinity to group tasks efficiently, but training MTL models for all task combinations is prohibitively expensive for large task sets.
approach: ETAP integrates gradient-based affinity scoring with trained non-linear predictors that correct residual errors, training on limited task groups with ground-truth MTL gain values.
contribution: Improves MTL gain prediction and enables more effective task grouping, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines across benchmark datasets in diverse application domains.
theme: Transfer Learning, Meta Learning, and Lifelong Learning

problem: Scattering transforms provide informative gradients for perceptual quality in inverse problems but are computationally expensive for use as differentiable loss functions during neural network training.
approach: SCRAPL proposes a stochastic optimization scheme for efficient evaluation of multiscale scattering transforms with importance sampling initialization adapted to dataset perceptual content.
contribution: Enables practical use of scattering transforms as loss functions for differentiable digital signal processing, demonstrated on unsupervised sound matching tasks.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models have high computational cost and low execution frequency, limiting suitability for real-time robotic and autonomous tasks requiring frequent action generation.
approach: SP-VLA jointly schedules models and prunes tokens by categorizing actions as deliberative or intuitive, dynamically switching between VLA and lightweight generator with spatio-semantic token pruning.
contribution: Reduces temporal and spatial redundancy in VLA models, achieving effective acceleration while maintaining focus on critical actions and salient visual information.

problem: Unsupervised domain adaptation struggles when target data are limited or spurious correlations dominate the source, requiring methods robust to both covariate and label distribution shifts.
approach: Proposes distributionally robust learning framework modeling uncertainty in covariate distribution and conditional label distribution, applicable to multi-source and single-source scenarios.
contribution: Provides efficient learning algorithm seamlessly integrated with existing UDA methods, consistently outperforming baselines especially when target data are extremely scarce.
theme: Transfer Learning, Meta Learning, and Lifelong Learning

problem: Unlearning methods for diffusion models remove target concepts but unintentionally suppress benign co-occurring concepts, preventing generation of related content.
approach: ReCARE explicitly safeguards co-occurring associated retained concepts (CARE) by automatically constructing a CARE-set from target images and leveraging it during unlearning training.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art balance of robust concept erasure, overall utility, and CARE preservation across multiple target concepts like nudity and artistic styles.

problem: Online video super-resolution methods using single previous frames for temporal alignment limit long-range temporal modeling and computational efficiency.
approach: TS-Mamba constructs trajectories within video to select similar tokens from previous frames, using shifted SSMs for spatio-temporal aggregation with trajectory-aware loss supervision.
contribution: Achieves SOTA performance compared to six benchmark methods by leveraging long-term trajectory modeling and low-complexity Mamba with Hilbert scanning-based spatial continuity.

problem: Cryptocurrency time series generation benchmarks neglect crypto-specific complexities like 24/7 trading, extreme volatility, and rapid regime shifts, limiting practical utility.
approach: CTBench evaluates TSG models across 13 metrics spanning forecasting, rank fidelity, trading performance, and risk assessment with dual-task framework for predictive utility and statistical arbitrage.
contribution: First cryptocurrency benchmark systematizing 452-token dataset evaluation across eight TSG methods, revealing trade-offs between statistical quality and trading profitability.

problem: Looped Transformers fix loop iterations during training and inference, preventing flexible computational budget adaptation for variable compute constraints.
approach: LoopFormer trains on variable-length trajectories with shortcut-consistency ensuring shorter loops yield informative representations while longer loops refine them via budget-conditioned reasoning.
contribution: Demonstrates robust performance under aggressive compute constraints while scaling gracefully with additional budget, enabling adaptive and controllable language modeling.

problem: Converting softmax attention Transformers to hybrid architectures interleaving linear attention requires selecting which layers to convert, with existing heuristics either uniform or layer-specific but inefficient.
approach: Uses layer importance scores derived from small generic text training for layer selection, followed by distillation via attention weight transfer, hidden state alignment, and KL matching.
contribution: Outperforms uniform interleaving and specialized diagnostic approaches for layer selection in distilling softmax Transformers to efficient hybrid attention architectures.

problem: Smooth activation functions like GELU allow negative pre-activations to carry signal and gradients, but neuron-level interpretability historically focuses on positive activations, overlooking their functional role.
approach: Studies Wasserstein neurons whose output distributions deviate from Gaussian baseline, demonstrating through targeted interventions that negative pre-activations differentiate syntax from semantics.
contribution: Sign-specific ablation of negative Wasserstein neurons increases perplexity and degrades grammatical performance, yielding a double dissociation between syntax and non-grammatical capabilities.

problem: Narrow training distributions for LLM feedback limit generalization without expensive diverse feedback collection, motivating methods to leverage feedback more effectively.
approach: Contrastive weight steering edits model parameters via weight arithmetic by subtracting weight deltas from opposing fine-tuning runs, enabling behavioral modification without full retraining.
contribution: Achieves stronger out-of-distribution control than activation steering while mitigating behavioral drift during fine-tuning, with preliminary evidence for detecting emergent misalignment via weight similarity.

problem: Game-theoretic economic models lack unified frameworks capturing both time and uncertainty with endogenous action sets, and lack scalable solution methods for infinite-horizon equilibria.
approach: Markov pseudo-games extend Markov games to allow players' actions to determine others' available actions, with polynomial-time convergence method for equilibrium computation.
contribution: Establishes existence of recursive Radner equilibria in infinite-horizon Markov exchange economies and enables computation via generative adversarial policy neural networks.

problem: Contrastive audio-text pretraining suffers from optimization trajectory drift caused by unconstrained negative sample repulsion, destabilizing training despite containing useful information.
approach: SVR introduces an auxiliary support vector to control the perpendicular component of negative sample pushing forces, with unsupervised strategies for semantic radius parameterization.
contribution: Surpasses InfoNCE and SigLIP losses on classification and multilingual retrieval with efficient implementation adding negligible overhead, with theoretical validation of trajectory drift mitigation.

problem: Schrödinger bridge algorithms require samples from both marginal distributions, but many applications provide one or both distributions only as unnormalized densities without sample access.
approach: Generalizes iterative proportional fitting to data-free case inspired by off-policy RL for diffusion sampling, learning the diffusion coefficient to improve data-to-data bridges.
contribution: First general method for Schrödinger bridges with unnormalized densities enabling sampling of posterior distributions in latent spaces of generative models without sample access.

problem: Causal structure recovery from dynamic data traditionally uses time-domain approaches, but the relative advantages of frequency-domain methods remain unclear for networks with dynamical dependencies.
approach: Analyzes Wiener Filter-based causal structure recovery in both time and frequency domains, establishing concentration bounds and leveraging FFT efficiency and phase properties.
contribution: Establishes that frequency domain provides distinct advantages for recovering Markov Equivalent Graphs in networks with dynamical dependencies through theoretical analysis.

problem: Offline multi-objective optimization faces generalization challenges beyond observed data with limited ways to explore the Pareto front without explicit surrogate models.
approach: PCD formulates offline MOO as conditional sampling problem, conditioning directly on desired trade-offs with reweighting strategy and reference-direction mechanism for Pareto front exploration.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on offline MOO benchmarks with greater consistency across tasks than existing approaches through direct trade-off conditioning.

problem: Interpreting transformer-based TCR-pMHC binding models remains challenging due to black-box encoder-decoder architectures, limiting mechanistic understanding of T cell immune response.
approach: QCAI quantifies cross-attention interactions in transformer decoders with TCR-XAI benchmark of 274 experimentally-determined structures for ground-truth physical distance validation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art interpretability performance on TCR-pMHC binding prediction while accurately estimating amino acid residue importance based on physical interaction regions.

problem: Visual prosthetics using microstimulation of early visual cortex are limited by electrode count, suggesting higher-level visual regions with complex object representations could enable richer experiences.
approach: Develops causally predictive models with topographic components and perturbation modules to guide optimal stimulation in higher-level cortex, with mapping procedure translating to primate anatomy.
contribution: Model-guided stimulation successfully steers complex visual behavior in macaques, establishing a foundation for next-generation prosthetics targeting higher-level visual cortex.

problem: Current RL techniques for LLM post-training may sharpen existing capabilities rather than discover truly novel behaviors, limiting expansion of model capabilities through exploration.
approach: Representation-based exploration uses diversity bonuses derived from pre-trained model hidden states for both inference-time and post-training, with principled representation-based diversity metrics.
contribution: Achieves 50%+ improvement in verifier efficiency at inference-time and 3x improvement in post-training sample efficiency on AIME 2024, matching higher-sample performance with fewer evaluations.

problem: Conventional atom-centric molecular models overlook complex bond-level phenomena like resonance and stereoselectivity, limiting predictive accuracy for nuanced chemical behaviors.
approach: DeMol uses dual-graph framework with parallel atom-centric and bond-centric channels fused by Double-Helix Blocks, with covalent-radii regularization for geometric consistency.
contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art on PCQM4Mv2, OC20 IS2RE, QM9, and MoleculeNet benchmarks through explicit bond-information modeling and intricate atom-bond interaction learning.
